newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF Knoll acquires group off Gehe.
newsitem.headline: BASF Knoll acquires group off Gehe.

text.p: Knoll AG, the drugs unit of German chemicals giant BASF AG, on Tuesday said that it has purchased French generic drug manufacturer GNR-pharma from German drugs wholesaler Gehe AG.
For BASF the acquisition marks another step in its efforts to expand its drugs unit, Knoll said in a statement.
Separately, Gehe earlier this morning said it planned to sell most of its pharmaceutical production units in order to concentrate more strongly on the wholesale business.
GNR-pharma, which specialises in heart, circulatory and dermatology drugs and is France's largest generic drugs group, is expected to post sales of around 60 million francs in 1996, Knoll said.
The French group expects to produce 10 new substances before the end of the year increasing the total of manufactured substances to 25, Knoll said.
Generic drugs are drugs whose patent expiry has lapsed and can often be sold for a lower price.
No one was immediately available to comment on how much BASF paid for GNR-pharma.
